title: Subgingival Proteome In Parents With Periodontitis And Their Offspring
projectDescription: This study evaluated the subgingival proteome of parents with periodontitis and their offspring, thereby assessing signatures of periodontal disease. Forty participants were allocated into four groups (n = 10 per group): parents with periodontitis (PP) and their offspring (CP), and control parents (PC) and their offspring (CC). Periodontal clinical parameters were assessed. Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) and subgingival biofilm were collected from the same sites. Proteome from GCF were investigated by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry with data-independent acquisition (DIA-PASEF).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Protein preparation and peptide extraction for mass spectrometry analysis was performed using a commercially available kit (PreOmics) with a modified version of the protocol (direct lysis). The desalted samples were analyzed on Evosep One Liquid Chromatography system coupled to a timsTOF Pro mass spectrometer. The peptides were subjected to label-free quantitative proteomics employing liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS) with data-independent acquisition (DIA)-mass spectrometry to dissect the proteome. The LC-MS analysis was performed in the positive-ion mode with dia-PASEF method.
dataProcessingProtocol: For analyzing diaPASEF data, the acquired data independent acquisition spectra processed with DIA-NN v.16, utilizing a library free approach with the following protein databases: UniProt human proteome and Human Oral Microbiome Database (eHOMD). P-values were adjusted using the Benjamini and Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate (FDR), considered at ≤1%.Differences were considered as statistically significant at fold-change ≥2, p value <0.05.
